text:
maria: FYI escalating a customer report — AcmeCorp seeing truncated streaming responses + frequent disconnects when using our /v1/stream endpoint behind their gRPC gateway -> nginx -> ALB chain. They say partial tokens arrive then stream cuts with 502 from the gateway. Repro steps attached below.

alex: thx. any sample request/headers from their side? is it pure SSE or grpc-web?

maria: they're using SSE (Accept: text/event-stream) from a browser client -> grpc-gateway (translates REST to gRPC) -> nginx (reverse proxy) -> ALB -> our hosted API (h2). Their gateway converts to HTTP/2 for our backend. They said it works fine if they hit our hosted endpoint directly, only fails via gateway path.

devon: common culprit is intermediary buffering / chunk coalescing or grpc-gateway doing response buffering until final chunk. nginx sometimes buffers (proxy_buffering on) and ALB has timeouts for idle streams. do we have their nginx conf? also need exact status codes and response body captured.

maria: pasted minimal repro from the customer below. they ran curl from inside their infra: 

```
curl -i -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  "https://their-gw.example.com/api/predict/stream?model=gpt-3.5" \
  --no-buffer
```

They said behavior: initial SSE lines arrive (data: {"choices":[{"delta":...}) then stream stops with gateway 502 and browser shows "connection reset". Server side logs show no error; our runtime shows stream closed by client after ~6s.

jin: can they capture tcpdump/nghttp2 logs between gateway and nginx/ALB? Also ask for the exact gateway component (gRPC gateway implementation) — some variants use grpc-web which wraps frames differently.

maria: customer sent header dump: 
```
GET /api/predict/stream HTTP/1.1
Host: their-gw.example.com
Accept: text/event-stream
Authorization: Bearer redacted
User-Agent: acme-stream-client/1.2
Connection: keep-alive
```

Between nginx -> ALB we see HTTP/1.1, but nginx forwards to backend with h2. Their nginx conf includes `proxy_http_version 1.1;` and `proxy_buffering on;` (ugh).

alex: that combination explains it. If nginx buffers the response it will try to collect enough bytes to satisfy buffer thresholds before flushing chunks to the client. For SSE/streaming you must set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` for HTTP/1.1 proxies, and ensure `Connection: keep-alive` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no` if using nginx accel. For h2 backends, chunked encoding isn't used — h2 has data frames — but nginx still has its buffering semantics.

devon: also confirm ALB type: classic ALB/ELB behaves differently from NLB. ALB (L7) can buffer and enforce idle timeouts (default 60s). If the gateway creates many short-lived reopens it can hit backend limits. Recommend switching to NLB for raw streaming.

maria: customer also observed "partial JSON lines" where SSE events contain truncated JSON (last char missing). They suspect chunk boundary issues.

jin: truncated JSON usually indicates chunk boundaries being cut mid-token by the proxy or the client closing before last bytes flushed. Another possibility: our runtime flush cadence is small and a proxy coalesces/repairs chunks causing incorrect content-length accounting when a proxy tries to set Content-Length on proxied response. We don't set Content-Length on streaming responses.

alex: can we confirm what headers our runtime emits for SSE? It should be: 
```
HTTP/2 200
content-type: text/event-stream; charset=utf-8
transfer-encoding: (absent for h2)
cache-control: no-cache
```
We rely on data frames over h2, not chunked-transfer-encoding. If an intermediary translates h2->http/1.1 it needs to convert h2 frames to chunked properly. If it fails, you'll see truncation.

maria: customer provided nginx error log snippet: 
```
2026/02/28 15:12:03 [error] 2412#0: *112 upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream, client: 10.0.1.12, server: their-gw, request: "GET /api/predict/stream HTTP/1.1", upstream: "http://internal-service:8080/api/predict/stream", host: "their-gw.example.com"
```

devon: "upstream prematurely closed" often means the upstream (could be ALB -> our API) reset the connection. But we saw our runtime logs say client closed after ~6s. Could be nginx/ALB closing the socket due to header/body length expectations.

sre-jordan: also check keepalive limits between nginx and ALB; if there is a proxy that doesn't support HTTP/2 persistent streams, the ALB might open a new connection per request and close too early. Also check for any 502 in ALB access logs with description "Idle connection timeout".

maria: customer also tried bypassing nginx and calling ALB directly (still via grpc-gateway) and saw improvement but still occasional truncation. Only direct hits to our endpoint are stable. So multiple intermediaries amplify fragility.

alex: propose triage plan: 
1) Ask customer to disable nginx proxy_buffering and set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on the route. Provide config snippet.
2) If they use ALB, ask them to inspect ALB access logs for GC/timeout/502 details; consider NLB or direct h2-enabled proxy.
3) Capture a raw h2 trace using `nghttp`/`nghttp2` from gateway to our backend if possible.
4) We (support) to collect our runtime logs for the exact request_ids/time range — ask for the request-id header they saw so we can correlate.

maria: sending config snippet now: 
```
location /api/predict/stream {
  proxy_pass http://internal-service:8080;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  proxy_set_header Connection "";
  proxy_buffering off;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  proxy_set_header X-Accel-Buffering no;
}
```

jin: also add `proxy_set_header TE "trailers";` if using h2 -> http/1.1 conversions and the gateway needs trailers. And make sure the grpc-gateway path isn't rewriting or aggregating responses.

maria: customer tried that config — they report improved stability but still saw one truncated event per ~200 streams. They captured a tcpdump and we saw FIN from nginx to ALB immediately after a 1–2 byte frame.

alex: that smells like a bug in the grpc-gateway or the ALB's http/2->http/1.1 translation where small final frames get cut. We should surface this to eng-runtime as a potential compatibility bug with intermediaries.

devon: please ask customer to run quick reproducer against our staging with similar chain so we can replicate. Provide a minimal Node script that streams SSE and leaves connection open for 30s: 
```
const http = require('http');
http.get('https://their-gw.example.com/api/predict/stream', {headers: {'Accept': 'text/event-stream'}}, (res) => {
  res.on('data', (chunk) => process.stdout.write(chunk));
  setTimeout(() => console.log('done'), 30000);
});
```

maria: I've requested request-id, tcpdump, nginx conf, ALB logs, and their repro script. They provided one request-id: req_20260228_az12_9987. Please correlate in logs.

support-bot: Note: support ticket #SE-1024 updated. Escalation to eng-runtime created: ER-447.

alex: I'll pick this up if they can reproduce against our staging endpoint via their gateway. If we can confirm a conversion bug we may need to document best-practice: prefer NLB or ensure h2-aware proxies (envoy/nginx with http2) and disable buffering.

maria: thanks all. I'll update ticket with the nginx config and ask for the staging reproducer run + pcap. Will ping again once we have staging repro. :thumbsup:

devon: one more note to include in guidance: explicitly add `Cache-Control: no-transform` for intermediaries that might try to alter content. Some proxies rewrite chunked responses otherwise.

maria: good call. adding that.

sre-jordan: if customer is enterprise, we can offer Private deployment or Dedicated route to avoid ALB/gateway issues. Flagging as advisory.

maria: closing loop here until we get more artifacts from customer. thanks team.
